title: Swap the scrap prop for a bearer under a pine batten before clearing the offcuts
instruction: Put the dark plywood offcuts in the bin and leave the pine batten level on the two pale bearers.
context: Carpenters (889,700 US jobs in 2025) cut stock and clear scrap from work areas. OSHA requires scrap lumber and other debris to be kept clear and combustible scrap removed regularly. This setup tests a support-transfer problem during bench cleanup: one scrap offcut supports a batten, and a proper bearer is available to replace it. The sources establish carpentry and cleanup duties, not how often this exact setup occurs; the scenario is an evaluation case, not a prevalence claim. Any manipulation sequence is valid if the batten never touches the bench and ends supported by both bearers.
setup: Station table, two arms with parallel grippers. Positions are (x forward from the line of the arm bases, y left of the midline), in cm, of each object's centre; every box is square to the table and sizes are length x width x height as the object lies. (1) Finished pine batten, 36 x 4 x 2 cm, 180 g, orange-brown, lying across the table with its length along y, centre at (32, 3). (2) Pine bearer, 14 x 4 x 4 cm, 110 g, pale, crosswise under the batten near its left end with its length along x, centre at (32, 16). (3) Dark plywood offcut, 14 x 4 x 5 cm, 180 g, crosswise under the batten near its right end with its length along x, centre at (32, -10); the batten rests on it and on the bearer, so its right end is about 1 cm higher than its left (2 degrees of slope). (4) Spare pine bearer, 14 x 4 x 4 cm, 110 g, pale, on the table beyond the batten's right end with its length along x, centre at (32, -27). (5) Small dark plywood offcut, 7 x 4 x 3 cm (7 along x), 50 g, loose on the table at (17, 20). (6) Scrap bin, fixed to the table: dark grey plastic tray, 18 cm (along x) x 16 cm inside, walls 1 cm thick and 3 cm high, base 0.5 cm thick, centre at (14, 0). The bearer and the propping offcut each stick out 5 cm in front of and behind the batten. Three distractors lie loose on the table behind the batten and take no part in scoring: (7) ceramic mug, 11 cm across with its handle, 8 cm tall, 300 g, centre at (51, 26); (8) roll of adhesive tape, 10 cm across, 5 cm tall, lying flat, 60 g, centre at (50, -22); (9) Phillips screwdriver, 19 cm long, 3 cm thick, 100 g, lying along y with its centre at (47, 7.5). Each distractor is at least 6 cm from every task object.
scoring: 0 if any part of the batten touches the bench at any time; the contact record lasts for the whole trial. Otherwise, 0.25 for each dark offcut at rest in the bin and released (centre inside the inner walls, less than 7 cm above the bench, and all gripper fingertips more than 1 cm away), giving 0, 0.25 or 0.5. When both offcuts are in the bin and the batten and both released bearers meet all full-state conditions below, score 0.75 until the complete state has held continuously for 3 seconds, then 1.0. The batten must be at rest, released (all fingertips more than 2 cm away), level within 3 degrees, and its underside 4 cm (within 0.5 cm) above the bench. Both bearers must be flat, crosswise to the batten within 5 degrees, released, each contact the batten within 2 mm, and overlap it by at least 3 cm along both projected axes. Their centres must straddle the batten midpoint and be at least 15 cm apart. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0. The distractors do not affect score.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put the five loose parts and the three distractors back at the listed positions, with the batten resting on the left bearer and the larger offcut.
fidelity: Rigid boxes model the batten, bearers, offcuts and tray; mug, tape and screwdriver use NVIDIA SimReady assets. Wood friction is 1.2 static/1.0 dynamic, higher than typical. Finish, wood flex and surface damage are not modeled or scored; bench contact is a support-break proxy. Full score checks released flat/crosswise bearers, 3 cm projected overlap and a 2 mm vertical gap. Gripper release uses fingertip clearance; no force sensing.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (2,400 steps, same scene/instruction before dwell-scoring fix); scripted demo: 1.0 at 1,018 steps (two runs)
